text.p: Dutch food group CSM NV said on Wednesday its 1995/96 net profit rose 8.1 percent and added that business in the current year was satisfactory.

CSM, whose main businesses include the making of sugar, dry goods, confectionery and other food ingredients, announced net profit in the year to end-September rose to 201.60 million guilders from 186.50 million the previous year.
Analysts had forecast net profit for the year at between 197 million and 216 million with consensus at 204 million.
"The progress of business in the current year is satisfactory," the company said in a statement with the full year figures. It gave no firm forecast for the 1996/97 year.

Operating profit pushed up to 293 million guilders from 269.70, largely reached through the strong increase in operating profit from the ingredients division, where the contribution from acquisitions was the most important factor.
Operating results from the sugar division and foodstuffs divisions increased modestly.

Turnover rose to 3.03 billion guilders from 2.72 billion. "The biggest part of the increase in net turnover came from the rise in turnover at the ingredients division," CSM said. It said the division saw a 32.4 percent increase in turnover to 1.15 billion guilders, boosted by acquisitions.
Turnover at foodstuffs climbed to 1.28 billion from 1.23 billion while the sugar division's turnover slipped to 604 million guilders from 624 million. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
